title: Desktop apps and tools
summary: RDP desktop access reuses the fixture display or restarts a session orphaned by sesman. The forwarded viewer trusts SSH host-key verification, bypasses the per-port RDP certificate cache, and retains reason-specific client diagnostics. Direct routes verify their certificates. Native Windows --view opens FreeRDP on the host's own RDP listener with no SSH run or XFCE probe, splits DOMAIN\user, follows the window size and reports desktop_session native; the YokeQa-ReturnToConsole task returns the console after the viewer closes. Linux and WSL desktop provisioning requires --browser-project and --browser-identity naming the operator identity. It registers yoke-identity-browser.desktop, whose Exec runs yoke browser open through bash -lc, as the http, https and text/html handler in mimeapps.list, so desktop links open signed in. Verify refuses linux_desktop_default_browser_not_selected when links bypass that launcher. Provisioning no longer installs snap Chromium or sets x-www-browser. Live host proof is still owed. On native Windows, yoke qa mission desktop lists, focuses, clicks, types into, presses keys in and reads any window through a hidden interactive scheduled task using Win32 input and UI Automation, with no RDP session; it verifies the foreground before input, reads typed text only from stdin and reports only its length, refuses secret or credential-shaped text, refuses options an action does not use, and names each failure (windows_desktop_locked, windows_window_not_found, windows_window_ambiguous, windows_element_ambiguous with --index N to pick a listed match, windows_foreground_refused). Other operating systems refuse desktop_input_unsupported_os and keep --gui-session osascript or xdotool.
